The important distinction for American readers is between the existence of a project and the availability of an edition to buy or read. Neither the official presentation nor the VIZ announcement gives a launch month, serial magazine, digital chapter platform, volume count or US license date for Shadow Rising. Search results that assign any of those details without a newer first-party citation are premature. This guide records the October reveal and the next named announcement opportunity rather than manufacturing a publication calendar.
The Team 7 teaser offers images rather than a full synopsis

The official description lists a sequence of storyboard-style images: six previous Hokage faces above the Hidden Leaf Village, a seventh stone face still being built, Naruto lifting the Hokage hat, a smiling Kakashi, Sasuke in a dignified pose and Sakura looking lovingly at a baby. The teaser ends with Naruto and Sasuke clashing. These images are meaningful because they point to a specific phase of the characters' lives, but an advertising montage is not a chapter outline.

One reasonable reading is that the project will revisit an interval connected with Naruto's path to becoming Hokage. Yet the material could use flashbacks, parallel sequences or symbolism, and the teaser does not clarify the narrative order. Sakura holding an infant is not a public confirmation of every character's age or the manga's precise timeline. USA Anime Club can analyze what the imagery suggests while explicitly separating it from a fact that the production has not published.
Why the seventh Hokage monument matters

The under-construction seventh face is a concrete clue in the teaser, not merely generic franchise iconography. The Hokage monument visually represents succession, public responsibility and Naruto's long pursuit of recognition. Showing a face being added can establish a transition between the role he once aspired to and the burden of occupying it. That is an editorial interpretation of the published image description rather than a claim about an unreleased chapter's ending.

Fans familiar with Boruto know that Naruto is already the village's Seventh Hokage in the sequel's main period. That background raises the possibility of a story situated earlier than parts of Boruto. But it does not establish an exact year, whether the manga is a prequel or whether the teaser's every scene appears literally in the finished work. The careful headline is about confirmed teaser material, not a promised hidden chronology.
Naruto and Sasuke facing off is deliberately ambiguous

The teaser's concluding confrontation is likely to attract theories because Naruto and Sasuke's rivalry has defined the emotional logic of the original series. A clash could imply an intense battle, a training exchange, a recollection or a symbolic confrontation staged for promotion. No verified announcement supplied dialogue, stakes, outcome or villain information alongside the image. Treating the frame as a future major betrayal would overstate its evidentiary value.

An appealing editorial angle is to contrast the visual idea of conflict with the preceding images of settled relationships and civic duty. The teaser may be asking readers to remember the friendship that made the rivalry meaningful. Yet even that remains an interpretation of marketing material. Until the manga is available, review websites should not present invented fight scenes, character deaths or chapter names as spoilers. There are no published Shadow Rising chapters to review as of this check.
What Kishimoto's role confirms and what it does not

The official Japanese announcement says Kishimoto is creating and drawing a new Naruto manga, an unusually strong signal about original-creator involvement. That should not be blurred with the separate credits for Boruto: Two Blue Vortex, where VIZ attributes creation and supervision to Kishimoto and ongoing art to Mikio Ikemoto. The teaser is an announcement of a distinct project, not evidence that Ikemoto is leaving Boruto or that Boruto's serialization is ending.

An author can supervise one franchise work and directly illustrate another, so those credits can coexist. What has not been confirmed is the scale of Kishimoto's new commitment: it could be a limited work or a larger ongoing manga. No page count, weekly schedule, named assistant staff or editorial publishing channel was disclosed. For readers trying to decide when to subscribe to a platform, the responsible answer is to monitor official publisher listings.
Is there a US English release date?

At the November 15, 2026 source check, VIZ has announced the project in US-facing editorial coverage but has not supplied a preorder listing, English ISBN, Chapter 1 URL or a dated serial release for Shadow Rising. A mention on a licensed publisher's news page is not a promise that simultaneous English chapters will be available from its app on an unstated day. Similarly, a trailer on the official YouTube channel is not a preview of finished, publicly readable pages.

Once Shueisha publishes a serialization announcement, American readers can check VIZ's Shonen Jump chapter directory and MANGA Plus for actual access, territory restrictions and whether the first chapter is free. Until those sources display the title and an eligible chapter, recommending an unauthorized scan site would not help anyone looking for a dependable English reading route. The series should remain on a release watchlist, not a live chapter index.
Jump Festa 2027 is the next announced checkpoint

Both the Japanese Naruto notice and VIZ's October statement point to Jump Festa 2027 for follow-up news. The event takes place December 19–20, 2026 at Makuhari Messe. The official Jump Festa program places the Naruto Jump Super Stage on Saturday December 19 from 16:55 to 17:25 Japan Standard Time. That is a confirmed stage slot, not a confirmed start time for any manga serialization.

For a US reader, the precise announcement may arrive overnight or early morning depending on the time zone; a translated press release could follow the Japanese stage. It is more useful to check the event's verified streaming information and the official Naruto or VIZ news account after the panel than to rely on social posts with screenshots whose context is unclear. Any real release date announced there would justify a substantive update to this article.
The right expectations for the next reveal

The most valuable next facts would be the manga's actual publication format, date, magazine or app, length and first English rights-holder listing. A detailed premise, complete chapter preview or creator interview would also clarify whether the Hokage imagery is a chronological clue or a promotional motif. None of those gaps should be filled by unsupported fan predictions. The confirmed October evidence is already sufficient to establish that Shadow Rising is a real, named new Naruto manga.

In practical terms, the story worth publishing now is the difference between what the teaser shows and what the publisher has yet to say. Kishimoto's direct drawing credit, the Team 7 imagery and the announced Jump Festa follow-up form the documented core. Keeping the original announcement date separate from later editorial check dates will also let readers recognize an authentic update when new details arrive, instead of encountering a silently refreshed rumor roundup.

sections: The four-episode crossover is a real production

The October 10 New York Comic Con panel introduced Naruto × Ninkū as a newly produced four-episode anime rather than an unofficial fan animation or a compilation of earlier television episodes. VIZ, the Naruto rights holders and a dedicated project website all refer to the collaboration. The official announcement says that Masashi Kishimoto and Ninkū creator Koji Kiriyama supervise the entire story. That is unusually direct evidence for an event-size anime project, even though the broadcast calendar is incomplete.

Four episodes describe the announced scope, not the release cadence. There is no authority for assuming a four-week Netflix drop, a simultaneous Crunchyroll premiere, or a specific US dub. A fan searching for the return of Team 7 can be confident the project exists but should not reserve a day to watch it until a Japanese distributor and authorized US platform publish their own listings.
Official premise: Kakashi gives Team 7 a mission

The special site's story introduction begins with a mission assigned to Naruto, Sasuke and Sakura by Kakashi. Since Kakashi cannot participate himself, Naruto is asked to act as leader of the three young ninjas. That situation brings out Naruto's eagerness to take responsibility, a recognizable feature of the earlier Team 7 era. During the mission the group becomes lost in another world. This description is confirmed by the production, not extrapolated from a trailer montage.

In that world, the team encounters Fūsuke, a boy with a face the official copy compares to a frog's. The premise establishes a meeting between characters created for two separate fictional universes, but stops short of explaining every rule of their journey. It does not confirm the identity of a main antagonist, how the group returns home, which jutsu will resolve the crisis or how a four-part narrative ends. A practical news guide should honor that boundary.
Why Ninkū is central rather than a guest appearance

Kishimoto has repeatedly identified Ninkū as an important influence on the creation of Naruto. His creator statement for this collaboration goes further, explaining that he wanted to see Ninkū continue and that Fūsuke serves as a hidden artistic mentor to Naruto. The crossover can therefore be understood as an encounter between a later franchise and an earlier work that helped shape its approach to martial action and personality-driven storytelling.

That context gives the collaboration a distinct identity. It is not merely a commercial pairing of two ninja brands with similar uniforms. Kiriyama's own comments describe the meeting of the two worlds as an event made possible through Kishimoto's proposal and cooperation. A compelling article can explain this documented creative relationship without claiming that every similarity between the manga is intentional or that the crossover permanently merges their canonical histories.
Production staff and what their credits actually mean

VIZ's announcement names Noriyuki Abe in a directing role and Tetsuya Nishio as a character designer and chief animation director, connecting the production to artists who worked on Naruto and Ninkū television animation. Crunchyroll's detailed coverage also lists Nozomi Fukui as assistant director, Hinatasho with a story credit, and music contributors Yasuharu Takanashi, -Yaiba- and Yusuke Honma. These are reported production roles, not a prediction of the animation's eventual quality.

The official promotional material includes a collaboration illustration and work-in-progress drawings. Such material is useful for judging the intended look, but it does not demonstrate that every episode is finished or guarantee that the final release will use exactly the same design in all shots. Fans should also distinguish the manga creators' supervision from hands-on direction and animation duties: those are separate creative functions, even within a work made to honor both original series.
Voices and the original Team 7 era

Junko Takeuchi, who voices Naruto in Japanese, and Noriaki Sugiyama, who voices Sasuke, appeared at the announcement event. The project's creator and cast comments emphasize the young-team period when Sasuke and Naruto still work together and Sakura accompanies them. That makes the early Naruto lineup an actual premise point rather than a fan guess based on promotional artwork. Ninkū actor Rica Matsumoto also shared a statement about the reunion with Fūsuke.

These confirmations do not by themselves list every speaking character in the crossover, guarantee a full English dub or provide a territory-by-territory voice cast. Someone hoping to hear an existing American dub cast should check an official US localization announcement when one is published. For now, it is accurate to discuss the Japanese cast context and the confirmed story premise, without promoting unsupported English voice actors as if they had been hired.
How it differs from the delayed 20th-anniversary Naruto anime

The number four can cause genuine confusion. In 2023, the Naruto anime committee planned four new anniversary episodes for consecutive weeks beginning September 3. Those were postponed on August 29, with the committee saying a revised broadcast schedule would be announced after additional production work. The 2026 Naruto × Ninkū reveal is a new, specifically titled crossover featuring a second franchise and the supervision of both manga creators.

Nothing in the October announcement says the Ninkū story is simply the older delayed production under a new name. Without an explicit rights-holder statement linking the two, readers should treat them as separate announced projects. The shared episode count is an interesting coincidence, not proof of identity. A separate comparison guide on USA Anime Club can show the two timelines and their different source pages for anyone trying to decide which trailer they have seen.
No release date or American streaming service yet

The dedicated Naruto × Ninkū official page describes its story and artistic rationale, but the records checked on November 15, 2026 do not supply a television debut day, weekly time, US streaming contract or simultaneous subtitle plan. Crunchyroll's coverage of the announcement also states that a release date was not announced at the panel. Reporting a launch as though the series were already watchable would therefore be misleading to US fans.

Once a distributor confirms its schedule, the details to capture are the Japanese broadcast date, US platform, local time, subtitling and dubbing plans, and whether all four parts are released at once. If a teaser is posted in English, that alone does not establish that the episodes will stream on the same YouTube channel. The correct current action is to follow the project's official news page and avoid unverified upload mirrors.
A crossover with a concrete creative purpose

The strongest reason to cover Naruto × Ninkū is not merely that Naruto is back in animation. The project formalizes an influence the original author has discussed for years: a character and creator who helped motivate his work now participate in an actual new story. The Team 7 assignment supplies a straightforward adventure setup, while Fūsuke's arrival connects the behind-the-scenes history to an on-screen meeting. That is a more distinctive editorial angle than repeating the trailer's character list.

The confirmed answer is concise: four episodes, a young Team 7 mission across worlds, both creators supervising and named production staff. The unfinished parts of the record are equally important: no verified premiere day or US streaming destination. Any future update should record who announced it and when, while keeping the separate anniversary episodes in their own historical entry. No conclusion about the eventual crossover's execution can be made until the episodes are actually released.

The Naruto franchise's March 9, 2023 announcement identifies Episode 293, scheduled for March 26 in Japan, as the conclusion of the first part of Boruto: Naruto Next Generations. That is an actual production confirmation, not a prediction based on manga popularity or a vague comment from a fan account. Its original date matters: the statement has existed for more than three years.

The announcement does not give a later premiere month. A 2023 promise of ongoing work is not proof that a television episode will air in 2026, and the absence of a published calendar is not proof of cancellation. Why Episode 293 is the essential reference point

Episode 293 is more than an arbitrary number in fan schedules. The production committee explicitly used that installment to mark the end of Part 1. That makes the number a reliable anchor when distinguishing available episodes from a future continuation. A streaming service might group the original television run into several seasonal menus, so its season label could differ from the committee's use of Part 1 and Part 2.

For Americans returning to the series, a sensible practical step is to verify that the episode collection actually reaches the Part 1 finale before searching for a new Part 2 tile. The official Naruto publication remains the trustworthy source for the original series boundary.
Part 2 and the Two Blue Vortex manga are not interchangeable

Boruto: Two Blue Vortex is the title of the continuing manga, which began after the first Boruto manga and its major change in chronology. VIZ's English chapter directory credits Masashi Kishimoto with creation or supervision and Mikio Ikemoto with art, and separately lists the currently released chapters. It is tempting to describe the next anime as Boruto: Two Blue Vortex because that would communicate a recognizable manga era. But the 2023 animation notice did not confirm the exact amount of manga to be adapted, the final television title or a chapter-to-episode mapping. A manga continuing through 2026 also does not establish the television studio's staffing or broadcast availability. These need independent anime production announcements.
What the October 2026 Project Rasengan roadmap changes

The Naruto franchise's New York Comic Con showcase introduced Project Rasengan, a multiyear plan across anime, manga, games and other activity. The currently public roadmap prominently includes the Naruto × Ninkū four-episode crossover, Kishimoto's Shadow Rising manga, a worldwide mobile-game expansion and the Naruto Card Game. Such a broad portfolio proves the franchise is pursuing several projects; it is not itself a dated Boruto anime premiere notice.

A reader should not substitute an October roadmap for the 2023 Boruto Part 2 announcement unless a future project box is explicitly identified as that continuation. The similarly branded anime and manga initiatives share creators, characters and business partners but have separate timelines. Even an official promotional event can mention a future anime project without disclosing which earlier promise it corresponds to. The precise wording of each rights-holder statement matters.
Why 2026 and 2027 return-date claims need scrutiny

A search for Boruto Part 2 often produces exact launch months, weekly times and episode counts. Those entries may be fan expectations based on studio workloads, circulating leaks or a site's automatically generated placeholder. None of them should be presented as a verified schedule unless a primary animation committee or authorized distributor has actually dated the new series. The March 2023 statement alone does not support an April 2027 date or a surprise November 2026 launch.

Being specific about uncertainty is useful, not evasive. One can confirm that work was announced and that the earlier episode run ended, while noting that official release timing remains open. Readers planning a watchlist benefit more from a clearly marked pending status than from a false countdown. Future coverage should link directly to a newer committee statement if the date is announced, rather than changing the article silently.
Studio Pierrot's involvement does not supply a calendar

Studio Pierrot has long been associated with Naruto and Boruto animation, and executives from Pierrot Films participated in the October 2026 franchise announcements. This is significant production context. It does not establish an episode count, a specific animation team for Part 2, a new directorial credit or whether the return will use a seasonal rather than continuous broadcast structure.

Those choices matter because production format can affect pacing and scheduling. However, treating a preferred format as confirmed would confuse criticism of the earlier anime with reporting about the new project. An accurate article can explain the questions fans want answered without asserting a timetable for recording voices, completing animation or booking a Japanese broadcast slot. No direct access to the studio's private production milestones is claimed here.
Where to monitor authorized US availability

The Naruto official site is the first destination for announcements about the production itself. For Americans, a separately verified listing from an authorized streaming distributor would be needed to establish US premiere timing, subtitles and any English dub. Even if a platform holds the original Boruto series, the future continuation's distribution terms and release hours are separate contractual facts. The 2023 notice establishes none of those details.

VIZ's chapter archive is useful for manga continuation, not a substitute for an anime stream. A reader who wants new Boruto story material now can follow the officially licensed Two Blue Vortex manga under its actual chapter-access rules, while recognizing that reading ahead may spoil a later adaptation. The medium and rights holder should be explicit in every article link to avoid misleading visitors looking for episodes.
The publication standard for the next major update

The next substantive news would be a confirmed television title, Japanese broadcast window, staff announcement, episode format, official trailer tied to Part 2, or US rights holder schedule. Each claim should be supported by its own dated source. A teaser whose only identification is Naruto × Ninkū should not be relabeled as a Boruto Part 2 trailer simply because it contains young Team 7 characters.

For now, the practical answer is straightforward: Boruto anime Part 2 was explicitly confirmed in March 2023 after the 293rd episode, but its premiere date remains unannounced in the official records examined on November 15, 2026. Project Rasengan shows a busy franchise, not a substitute release date. Preserving that distinction gives fans a reliable status check and keeps future editorial updates tied to genuine developments.

The official casting announcement identifies Naruto Uzumaki, Sasuke Uchiha and Sakura Haruno as the three young characters the filmmakers are seeking. Those are the original Team 7 students at the heart of the franchise's early relationships. The global scope of the search is important because it means the selection process was not described as limited to an already chosen Hollywood shortlist. Casting for additional characters would follow, according to the July announcement.

A search is not proof that one particular actor has signed a contract. Social media speculation often assigns names to the roles based on resemblance or existing fan edits. A responsible coverage page must distinguish an officially announced casting process from confirmed performers, negotiations and fan suggestions. Until Lionsgate or the production identifies the selected actors, a headline proclaiming a particular Naruto or Sakura would be premature. The roles are confirmed; the performers remain an open question.
What Destin Daniel Cretton brings to the project

Destin Daniel Cretton is the filmmaker publicly attached to direct the Naruto live-action movie. His comments emphasize the importance of the original characters' bonds and the experience of discovering Kishimoto's story. Those remarks are more useful than an unsupported assurance that every famous battle will appear. The film will need to introduce a large fictional world while allowing a general audience to understand Naruto's personal motives and his connection to Team 7.

The official record does not yet explain how much manga material the first film will adapt, whether the story will use a single movie or several, or exactly how its action will translate ninjutsu into live photography and visual effects. A director's enthusiasm is a statement of intent, not a finished script breakdown. Fans can evaluate that intent without confusing it with verified shooting footage or a published scene list.
Kishimoto's support is real, but not a script credit

Masashi Kishimoto contributed a public statement supporting Cretton's involvement and expressing excitement about the chance to see actors embody his characters. That endorsement is meaningful because it comes from the original manga creator through the official franchise website. It does not mean he has been identified as the movie's screenwriter, director of photography or actor selector. Credits for story authorship, script development and on-set supervision are different facts.

It is also important not to turn creator approval into a guarantee that an adaptation will satisfy every fan. Translating a manga's long-form character development into a feature film requires decisions about omitted material, setting and tone. Those choices cannot be judged from a casting announcement alone. A future article about adaptation fidelity should examine a completed script synopsis, trailer or movie, rather than deriving scenes from Kishimoto's enthusiastic statement.
Charles Melton and Kakashi: reported talks versus final casting

On August 20, 2026, entertainment trade reporting said Charles Melton was in final discussions to portray Kakashi Hatake. TheWrap described the actor as in talks and noted that Lionsgate had not commented on the report. That is a legitimate piece of reported industry news, but the phrase final talks must not be rewritten into a confirmed casting credit. Talks can result in a deal or end without one, and a major role might remain unfilled publicly even when negotiations are advanced.

This matters because Kakashi is the leader associated with Team 7, but he is not one of the three younger lead roles in the original global casting announcement. Treating the casting search and the Melton report as the same kind of evidence would mislead readers. The former is an official franchise announcement; the latter is a sourced trade report of negotiations. Readers should look for a subsequent signed-deal announcement before assuming that any fan-art cast poster is accurate.
Why no release date has been verified

A studio-backed movie can take substantial time to move from announced pre-production to shooting and theatrical scheduling. A film calendar depends on casting, script completion, locations, visual effects work and marketing decisions. The July and October Naruto announcements did not identify a premiere year, an exact opening weekend or a streaming service that will receive the film later. An online claim that the movie releases on a certain holiday in 2027 therefore lacks support from the reviewed primary records.

A better way to track the project is to separate milestones: lead casting confirmed, production start, production completion, teaser release and official date announcement. Those are different events, and not all must occur publicly in the same order. USA Anime Club should update this page when a responsible rights holder publishes one, rather than treating social chatter about a possible trailer as a release announcement.
How this differs from Naruto animation news

The October 2026 franchise announcements also featured the new Naruto × Ninkū anime and Project Rasengan. Those are animated and cross-media initiatives, not new information about the live-action movie's theatrical release date. Sharing the Naruto brand does not collapse their budgets, teams or production stages. The four-episode crossover has its own supervision and studio roles, while the movie is led by Lionsgate and Cretton.

A reader searching for a new Naruto episode could easily arrive at a live-action headline, so the article should identify the medium in its title and answer. The cinema project also has no verified connection to the 2023-delayed four-anniversary-episode animation schedule. Keeping these projects on separate pages protects the user experience and allows genuine updates without conflicting information.
What the next confirmed film announcement should answer

The most useful next details are signed cast names with roles, a production start announcement, a synopsis that establishes the adaptation's scope, and an official theatrical date. A first trailer would also provide evidence about costume design and how ninja action is presented. A reputable casting report can be included with its uncertainty, while a verified studio announcement should take priority when it resolves that uncertainty.

As of November 15, 2026, the dependable summary remains Lionsgate pre-production, Cretton directing, global searches for Naruto, Sasuke and Sakura, Kishimoto's public encouragement and a reported but not finalized Kakashi negotiation. A publication serving US fans should offer those verified distinctions rather than a fantasy dream-cast grid presented as fact. The article's modified date should advance only when new material is actually added.

sections: A franchise roadmap, not the title of one anime

Project Rasengan was introduced during New York Comic Con on October 10, 2026 as a long-term international initiative for Naruto and Boruto. VIZ's US press release describes it as a plan across manga, animation, games and additional activities, accompanied by a promotional film and a graphic roadmap. The official landing page groups announced projects into separate modules. That makes Project Rasengan an umbrella for several works, not the title of a single television season.

This matters for search results. Someone encountering the phrase Project Rasengan anime release date may actually be asking about Naruto × Ninkū, while a card collector is interested in a June 2027 launch. A general roadmap article should guide readers to those distinct facts and avoid assigning one date to the entire project. Each component has its own producer, medium and announcement status.
Confirmed component: Naruto × Ninkū

The announced anime component is Naruto × Ninkū, a four-episode original crossover supervised by Naruto creator Masashi Kishimoto and Ninkū creator Koji Kiriyama. Its confirmed premise sends young Team 7 on a mission into another world where they encounter Fūsuke. The project has a dedicated official website with the story introduction and creator comments, so it is more substantive than a single mystery panel on a roadmap slide.

Nevertheless, Project Rasengan's existence does not provide a Japanese broadcast premiere, a Netflix date or a confirmed US streaming service for the crossover. A full story synopsis beyond the official introduction and claims about future guest characters would be speculation. Fans should follow the crossover-specific page for episode availability, because a multiyear marketing campaign can continue even while a particular anime has no public broadcast schedule.
Confirmed component: the Shadow Rising manga

New Naruto: Shadow Rising manga by Masashi Kishimoto is another revealed component. The Japanese Naruto announcement identifies the title and describes teaser images involving the Hokage monument and members of Team 7. The official Project Rasengan page presents it as a new story drawn by Kishimoto. That is a distinct creative promise from his supervision role on Boruto: Two Blue Vortex, which uses Mikio Ikemoto's ongoing art.

Shadow Rising has not been assigned an official serial publication day, issue number, collected-volume date or licensed US Chapter 1 URL in the records checked. The teaser's dramatic images are not an invitation to create fictional chapter summaries. More information is promised at Jump Festa 2027 in December. The manga article can explain the teaser in detail, while this roadmap guide focuses on how it fits into the wider set of announced projects.
Confirmed component: a worldwide Naruto Card Game

Bandai has confirmed that the Naruto Card Game will launch internationally in June 2027. The planned opening product family includes three preconstructed starter decks built around Naruto, Sasuke and Gaara, as well as an initial booster set. Official materials describe tactical card play using leaders, shinobi and chakra. Unlike a speculative roadmap box, this project has its own product website and a concrete worldwide launch month.

That does not establish every local store's inventory, retailer price or exact shipment day. June 2027 is the official release window, not permission to invent a Saturday on the calendar or a presale quantity. Demo activities have been announced for earlier in 2027, but participation can depend on stores and event eligibility. A card guide should provide those practical distinctions, leaving the broader Project Rasengan page focused on the franchise-wide chronology.
Confirmed component: Naruto Mobile expansion

The existing Naruto Mobile action game has operated in mainland China since 2016. The October 2026 showcase announced plans to take it worldwide, accompanied by promotional material and promised future updates. The project is listed on the official Rasengan page as a game that will expand internationally rather than an entirely unannounced new television series. Its release plan is commercially meaningful because American players have long encountered a Chinese-language market version.

The announcement includes important limitations. An exact global rollout date was not provided, supported languages have not been finalized publicly, and the franchise's note says availability may vary by country or region. That means a worldwide initiative is not identical to a guarantee that a particular US app store will contain the game on a stated day. Read the individual game guide for practical checks before installing any purported early APK or unofficial client.
The blank roadmap slots are intentionally unresolved

Promotional roadmaps can imply a great deal through empty panels, silhouettes and future years. Project Rasengan's 2026 announcement indicated that additional projects were still unannounced. It is reasonable to say that the franchise has more plans than those already named. It is not reasonable to label a blank space Boruto Season 2, a Hollywood sequel or a specific game expansion without an official identification.

Nor should a general 2027–2029 planning graphic be treated as an episode calendar. A block positioned near a year may represent a broad investment horizon rather than a premiere or publication day. Until the rights holder assigns text and a date to that position, a reader has only an open question. That distinction prevents the error of turning an attractive promotional graphic into apparently precise but invented journalism.
Where Boruto anime Part 2 fits—and does not fit

The Boruto anime committee announced Part 2 as in production in March 2023 after identifying Episode 293 as the first part's finale. That is a separate primary-source fact. The October 2026 Project Rasengan announcements name a new Naruto crossover, manga and games, but do not set a confirmed Boruto Part 2 premiere date in the materials examined. A roadmap carrying both Naruto and Boruto branding is not sufficient to resolve the television continuation's schedule.

Anyone searching for the Boruto return date should consult the standalone anime status report, which cites the actual committee statement. Manga publication under the Two Blue Vortex title continues through VIZ's English chapter service and has different release rules. Combining an ongoing manga with an old production announcement and an unlabeled promotional slot would create a false schedule even if the three facts are each individually genuine.
Jump Festa 2027 as the next editorial checkpoint

The official Naruto announcements point readers to Jump Festa 2027 for follow-up reveals. The event runs December 19–20, 2026; the published program places the Naruto stage on Saturday December 19 from 16:55 to 17:25 Japan Standard Time. That is a reliable time for checking actual public announcements, not a guaranteed launch of every project shown on the October roadmap.

A useful publication strategy is to maintain a source-linked register of which projects have named titles, rights holders, dates and US availability. When the December stage changes one of those fields, update the corresponding focused article and this overview with a new verified modified timestamp. Readers then receive a coherent family of guides instead of eleven announcements that all imply the same release date or invent details to fill every open roadmap box.

sections: Why people are confusing two four-part Naruto projects

Two unrelated dates in Naruto's recent production history can look suspiciously similar in a search snippet. In 2023, the anime committee announced four completely new episodes for the original television series' twentieth anniversary, and later postponed that plan. In October 2026, the franchise announced Naruto × Ninkū as a newly produced four-episode crossover. Both involve familiar young Naruto-era characters and both use the number four, but the official announcements do not say they are the same production.

That distinction is the key answer to the question. It is fair to acknowledge that fans may ask whether one project was repurposed into the other. What is not supported is a categorical assertion about internal assets, budgets or production reuse. No primary record examined identifies the 2026 collaboration as the revised release of the older 2023 anniversary series. Treating them separately is the most accurate reading of the available evidence.
The original anniversary plan in July 2023

The official July 23, 2023 Naruto notice introduced a four-week broadcast beginning September 3 on TV Tokyo-affiliated Japanese channels. Its teaser visual showed Naruto, Sasuke, Sakura and Kakashi from the pre-Shippuden Team 7 period. The announcement also described planned anniversary music: FLOW's newly recorded version of GO!!! and a cover of the familiar Viva☆Rock song. This was marketed as new animation honoring the original anime's twentieth anniversary.

Those concrete details are not interchangeable with a later crossover trailer. The original promotion did not present Fūsuke or Ninkū as story elements, and its scheduling information belonged to September 2023. Anyone finding that older official article today should notice the appended postponement warning, rather than treating the initial day and hour as a still-valid future airing plan.
The August postponement was explicit

On August 29, 2023, the Naruto anime production committee announced that the four-week anniversary series would not air on its originally planned date. It said additional time would be used to improve quality and promised to issue a revised broadcast schedule once finalized. The statement also described replacement programming: selected Boruto episodes would occupy the planned television slot. That is a clear historical postponement record.

The notice did not set a new premiere day or announce that the anniversary project had become a crossover with another franchise. A postponed broadcast is not identical to a cancelled production, but neither can it be reported as completed or released without later confirmation. As of the November 2026 records checked here, this primary statement remains the basis for distinguishing the delayed 2023 initiative from new projects announced years afterward.
The 2026 Naruto × Ninkū announcement is more specific

The October 2026 New York Comic Con event unveiled an original Naruto × Ninkū crossover anime with a named story concept. Naruto, Sasuke and Sakura receive a mission from Kakashi, Naruto serves as temporary leader, and the group wanders into another world where Fūsuke appears. Both Masashi Kishimoto and Ninkū creator Koji Kiriyama oversee the story. The official franchise has created a dedicated project page describing these roles and the premise.

This is a different package of information from the 2023 anniversary tease. It has an explicit second franchise, a creative collaboration and a narrative introduction. The production team also identified staff members associated with Naruto and Ninkū animation. The 2026 statement does not, however, provide a confirmed broadcast date or a US streaming platform. Both projects thus remain distinct in description while having different unresolved schedule questions.
Could the studios share work behind the scenes?

Fans may reasonably wonder whether animation prepared for a 2023 anniversary celebration was later recycled into a 2026 crossover, particularly because the recognizable young Team 7 appears in both promotions. That would be an interesting production question, but the public announcements do not establish it. Sharing a studio, character designer or franchise identity is not documentary evidence that scenes, storyboards or episode masters have been repurposed.

An answer would require a direct statement by the production committee or staff about the relationship between the projects. Without it, the safest formulation is that the two have not been officially identified as identical or as a rebranding. A responsible entertainment publication should not convert coincidental episode counts into a confident behind-the-scenes narrative, even when speculation has spread widely.
A straightforward evidence comparison for fans

The 2023 project has a known purpose: celebrating the original television anime's twentieth anniversary with four weeks of new programming. Its last definite schedule event in the cited record is an August postponement. The 2026 project has a known story: a four-episode crossover of Naruto and Ninkū created with both manga authors' supervision. Its announcement was at New York Comic Con and its specific premiere timing was not revealed.

These are separate fields, and keeping them separate removes most confusion. Neither statement announces an English dub release on Netflix. Neither gives a basis for calling the entire Boruto Part 2 continuation a four-episode special. Likewise, a later Project Rasengan page listing Ninkū does not automatically update the deferred 2023 schedule. A comparison article works precisely because it resists collapsing every Naruto animation headline into one imagined release.
How to recognize each teaser correctly

A promotional image containing young Team 7 is not enough to identify the project. For the delayed anniversary work, compare the 2023 official teaser and the music announcement tied to its former September slot. For Naruto × Ninkū, check the later official project site for the crossover logo, Fūsuke's appearance and the other-world mission introduction. A date and source link should accompany any reposted clip used as evidence.

The same care applies to headlines about Naruto's live-action movie or the Shadow Rising manga. They are different media projects, however similar their character portraits might look. A short caption identifying the precise source, year and production title helps prevent a reader from believing a nostalgic teaser announces a brand-new streaming premiere.
What would settle the outstanding question

The decisive evidence would be a clear rights-holder notice specifying whether the 2023 anniversary episodes remain separately planned, have been cancelled or have been incorporated into another named work. Absent that notice, the correct status for the original production is an announced postponement with no replacement broadcast date established here. A newer Ninkū premiere announcement would update only that crossover unless it explicitly explained the older series.

For US fans, the practical conclusion is that Naruto has two documented four-episode announcements from different years, not one confirmed release calendar. The first was postponed after a September 2023 plan; the second is a distinct 2026 creative crossover announcement. USA Anime Club should maintain different links and timestamps for both rather than suggesting the shared episode total proves they are secretly the same thing.

sections: The correct sequence in one sentence

Read Boruto: Naruto Next Generations from Chapter 1 through Chapter 80, then begin Boruto: Two Blue Vortex at its Chapter 1 and continue forward. VIZ's official US chapter directories list these as two separately titled parts of the same broader sequel story, with the original series ending at eighty chapters. The numbering resets for the continuation, so a new Chapter 1 does not erase the earlier eighty installments. Readers should finish the first series before starting the second if they want the narrative revelations in order.

The collected editions follow the same structure. Boruto: Naruto Next Generations has twenty English volumes, while Two Blue Vortex begins its own volume sequence with Volume 1. When an online store recommends Boruto Volume 1, check the full title: a book labeled Two Blue Vortex Volume 1 begins much later in the story than the Naruto Next Generations first volume. Matching the series title matters at least as much as matching the number.
Where Naruto itself fits before Boruto

Boruto follows Naruto's son and a new generation of Hidden Leaf shinobi, so the original Naruto manga provides substantial context about the village, older characters and relationships. VIZ's Naruto catalog ends at Chapter 700 and offers the first series as its own reading experience. If you want the complete chronological background, begin with Naruto before moving to Boruto: Naruto Next Generations. That is the most comprehensive approach for someone new to this fictional world.

However, Boruto's opening chapters introduce the young protagonist and his immediate setting, so a reader who already knows the broad Naruto premise can begin directly with Boruto. The essential requirement for avoiding sequel confusion is that Two Blue Vortex is not an introductory manga designed to stand entirely apart from Naruto Next Generations. Readers will encounter major consequences of prior events from its very first volume. Which earlier franchise side stories to read is a matter of interest, not a compulsory numbered prerequisite supplied by VIZ.
Why Chapter 80 is the real dividing line

VIZ's English chapter archive lists Boruto: Naruto Next Generations through Chapter 80. Its Volume 20 product page describes a crucial reversal affecting Boruto and Kawaki, making that final book a natural bridge into the next title. The important transition involves a change in how the protagonists are perceived and a shift in their circumstances. The sequel begins after those developments rather than restoring every relationship to the old status quo.

A spoiler-light guide can identify the break without narrating every detail of the reversal. If you want the surprise to land in the intended order, finish the original chapters instead of opening a summary of Two Blue Vortex first. The edition transition is particularly confusing in digital stores because both series may appear together under a general Boruto brand. The author's name is not sufficient to distinguish them; use the full series title and chapter count.
The reset: Two Blue Vortex Chapter 1 is not a reboot

VIZ's official Two Blue Vortex Volume 1 synopsis presents a Boruto who has been forced away from the Hidden Leaf Village and is training with Sasuke before returning amid new threats. This is continuation after a major shift, not a separate retelling of the first academy chapters. The new title and chapter numbering make it accessible as a publishing unit, but they do not erase the causes of its characters' circumstances.

Someone following individual chapters should select the Two Blue Vortex series directory after completing the original Chapter 80. Starting from the newer book's Chapter 1 is correct only after that transition. Online comments sometimes call it Boruto Part 2; that is useful casual shorthand for the manga, but should not be confused with the separate Boruto anime Part 2 production announcement. The formats and the production schedules are independently maintained.
Volumes and individual chapters are different products

A collected paperback groups chapters that previously appeared in serialization; an online chapter listing gives access to individual installments on a different release cycle. VIZ lists the US English Naruto Next Generations Volume 20 as a 216-page paperback released August 6, 2024. Two Blue Vortex Volume 1, by contrast, is a separate 184-page paperback released February 4, 2025. Those dates are publication records for the books, not the original online debut dates of every chapter inside them.

Readers building a shelf should follow the numbered volumes within each of the two series, while digital readers can follow the published chapter indexes. A bookstore may show the newest imported Japanese volume before its English edition is released; that does not mean the English publisher is missing chapters without explanation. Make sure the language, format and ISBN correspond to your actual buying goal.
Where US readers can read legally in English

VIZ publishes official English Shonen Jump chapter pages for both Boruto series. Its directories also direct readers to MANGA Plus by Shueisha for certain free chapters, while additional chapters may require joining the service. Access conditions can vary by episode or account and change over time. The presence of several free introductory chapters does not guarantee the entire archive can be read for free forever or downloaded as files.

To follow the story, open the official Naruto Next Generations chapter directory and finish through Chapter 80 using whatever licensed access applies to your account. Then navigate to the separate Two Blue Vortex index and begin with its Chapter 1. If you prefer purchasing books, choose the VIZ volume listings under the correct title. Avoid reading on an unlicensed mirror when the legitimate publisher provides a clear sequence.
Manga and anime numbers should not be interchanged

The Boruto: Naruto Next Generations anime ran to Episode 293 before Part 1 ended in 2023. That episode number is not a reference to manga Chapter 293. Television adaptations can add original storylines, rearrange events or divide arcs in ways that do not match the manga's collected edition boundaries. A viewer trying to continue directly from the anime should establish what story has actually been adapted before selecting an exact manga handoff point.

This guide deliberately does not manufacture a universal episode-to-chapter conversion. The safe manga reading order is clear independently of the television adaptation, and the future anime's release date remains a separate unresolved question. Readers who want to avoid missing character development can start with the earliest manga chapters rather than rely on a guessed point derived from episode numbering.
How to check that you're on the right page

A reliable chapter page should display both the title and the installment number. The original listing reads Boruto: Naruto Next Generations, while the continuation reads Boruto: Two Blue Vortex. The first ends at Chapter 80; the second begins at Chapter 1, and its newer chapter entries continue to appear independently. A third-party app might abbreviate these labels to Boruto, which makes a verified VIZ URL a useful reference.

The one-line answer for a US reader is original twenty-volume Boruto series first, then Two Blue Vortex from its own first volume or chapter. This approach keeps the timeline, the numbering reset and the purchase model distinct. The guide should be revised only if the publisher changes its access terms or issues a meaningful edition correction, not to artificially refresh its modified date every month.

sections: The current official credit line settles the central question

VIZ's current English Two Blue Vortex chapter directory credits Masashi Kishimoto with creation and supervision, and Mikio Ikemoto with artwork. Those are the most dependable public labels for the continuing manga as of November 15, 2026. A reader trying to identify the person drawing Boruto's current appearances should look to Ikemoto, not to Kishimoto's direct drawing work on the original Naruto manga. The source does not list the same person in both roles.

That distinction is often lost in social media shorthand. Calling a comic Kishimoto's Boruto may refer to his original world and supervisory role, while claiming Kishimoto personally draws every Two Blue Vortex chapter is a different and unsupported statement. A publisher's credit line is more useful than assumptions formed from which artist's style a reader prefers. The question is not which name is more famous; it is what the authorized edition actually attributes to each contributor.
Kishimoto created Naruto before supervising Boruto

Masashi Kishimoto wrote and drew the original Naruto manga, establishing its central characters and world long before the sequel began. His position in Boruto is therefore rooted in authorship of the franchise itself. VIZ uses the phrasing creation or supervision on the sequel's present listings. That is a role related to overall story direction and creative oversight, rather than an automatically comprehensive statement about who draws panels or pens each line of dialogue.

Credits describe an approved collaborative structure but may not expose the private workflow of draft revisions, editorial meetings or assistants. It would be misleading to infer that Kishimoto personally writes every speech balloon on a particular page merely from the words creation or supervision. Conversely, it would also be inaccurate to claim he has no creative involvement because another artist is publicly credited. The reliable answer preserves the distinctions the publisher chose.
Ikemoto is the ongoing Boruto manga artist

Mikio Ikemoto is credited by VIZ as the artist for both Boruto: Naruto Next Generations and Boruto: Two Blue Vortex. His work supplies the sequel's visual identity, from the main characters' designs to page layouts and action illustration. The published volume listings maintain this attribution across the first and second manga titles. A separate Shadow Rising project drawn by Kishimoto does not transfer Boruto's art responsibilities to him by implication.

Readers can reasonably compare Ikemoto's style with Kishimoto's original Naruto work as a matter of criticism. However, the existence of those stylistic differences is not evidence of an unannounced artist replacement. A good analysis should discuss composition and character design with examples from authorized pages, rather than pretend that an artist's visibility determines whether his contributions deserve credit. The two manga have related worlds but distinct artistic production.
Ukyo Kodachi's early script contribution matters

The original Boruto manga was initially associated with a team that included scriptwriter Ukyo Kodachi. VIZ's legacy listing explicitly carries the script credit, alongside Kishimoto's creation or supervision and Ikemoto's art. It is therefore inaccurate to erase Kodachi from the early manga history or to apply present-day credits backward as though no change ever occurred. Early Boruto chapters and later Two Blue Vortex issues should be contextualized within their respective production periods.

This is particularly relevant when readers compare the storytelling before and after a major transition. A change in script responsibility may influence tone or structure, but claims of direct causation need supporting evidence and close reading. One cannot assert that every creative decision was made by a single person just because the public credit arrangement changed. The first step is to identify accurately who is named in the editions and when.
The 2020 announcement changed the story-writing arrangement

Contemporaneous reporting of the franchise's November 2020 communication says the Boruto manga production system would change around Chapter 52, with Kishimoto's original drafts becoming the basis for the continuing story. Kodachi's tenure in the script role was recognized as the series moved into this arrangement. That historical record is important because it explains why older product pages may include Kodachi while current Two Blue Vortex entries center Kishimoto and Ikemoto.

Some English headlines summarized the development as Kishimoto taking over writing.
